input: # DELIBERATELY RED. See ../AGENTS.md, "The one exception".
# Every row here is input that RFC 8259 requires a parser to REJECT, that
# BOTH platform parsers (JSON.parse and encoding/json) reject, and that one
# of the two runtimes currently ACCEPTS. The rows pin the CORRECT behaviour
# so the gap cannot be quietly forgotten; they are expected to fail until
# the parsers are fixed (a later phase -- phase 1 only measures).
# Do not delete rows, relax the codes, or move the file out of the
# auto-discovery glob to get green. A red test is an honest test.
# Provenance: found by grading against nst/JSONTestSuite @
# 1ef36fa01286573e846ac449e8683f8833c5b26a (see scripts/fetch-jsontestsuite.sh).
# The corpus itself is not committed; these rows are the distilled defects.
# --- Group A: FAILS IN TYPESCRIPT (Go already rejects all of these) ---
# Trailing content after a complete top-level value is silently DISCARDED.
# This is data loss, not mere laxness: `"a" "b"` parses as "a".
# Corpus: n_structure_array_with_extra_array_close
# Corpus: n_structure_object_followed_by_closing_object
# Corpus: n_array_extra_close
# Corpus: n_array_comma_after_close
# Corpus: n_structure_close_unopened_array
# Corpus: n_structure_object_with_trailing_garbage
{"a": true} "x"
# Not in the corpus; the same defect, reduced.
a "b"
null null
# --- Group B: FAILS IN GO (TypeScript already rejects both of these) ---
# A non-string object key is accepted and coerced to the empty string:
# {1:1} parses as {"":1}, so the key is silently destroyed.
# Corpus: n_object_non_string_key
# Corpus: n_object_repeated_null_null
{null:null,null:null}
# Not in the corpus; the same defect, reduced.
{true:1}
